withdrawn_images.why: DEFECTIVE — must not run. Deterministic pre-init watchdog defect: with flags.bit1 = 1 the IDENT frame's kick called XScuWdt_RestartWdt on an instance not yet CfgInitialize'd (BaseAddr 0, IsReady unset), and the driver's assert waits forever — the image hangs after IDENT, before the opening baseline. Found in the owner's compatibility review 2026-09-01 (blocker 1); never run on hardware. Fixed by gating the kick on S.wdt_started, set only after CfgInitialize → SetControlReg → LoadWdt → Start, with init failure fail-closed.

DEFECTIVE — must not run. The rec-v3 batch's first candidate (2026-09-01): its bounded receive bounded only the FIRST byte of a host line and then blocked for the newline, so a RECACK/RECGET cut mid-line (tail and newline lost) would have held the application until the watchdog reset instead of resending and STOP_REC as designed (owner's review 2026-09-02, blocker 1 of four: also a broken resend of an accepted record was re-acknowledged on its header alone, PASS condition 7 was not machine-enforced, and two text/implementation gaps). Never run on hardware; never board-ready. Corrected by p3_rectx_recv_line (whole-line bound, pure, host-driven with truncated input) and the three host-side fixes; rebuilt as the next candidate.

DEFECTIVE — must not run. The rel-v4 firmware batch's first candidate (2026-09-03), never run on hardware; the owner's full P3 compatibility review (2026-09-03) found: (1) p3_pull.c accepted an AUDITDONE with zero or partial chunks served (the host's DONE was taken as the audit's completion whatever had been served: `audited` marked, ARM reachable, on an incomplete audit) — fixed: a DONE before every chunk was served aborts the pull fail-closed (no `audited`, no ARM), with C and Python negative tests (zero and 7/8 chunks); (2) the timed receiver's whole-line tick bound was idle_ticks × 4 = 32 s, so a host line trickled in below the idle gap could hold the application 4× the 8 s bound — fixed: line_ticks = idle_ticks (the ×4 factor stays on the poll count backstop only), with a source-derived audit and an injected-clock trickled-line counterexample; (3) AUDITWAIT.served counted transmissions (chunks_served) instead of unique chunks — fixed: popcount(served_mask), equal to `chunks` in the all-served branch, with a repeated-GET counterexample. The corrected image is 5deee74c… (the candidate entry at the time; promoted to pinned_at_build 2026-09-03).

bound_contract.whole_line: the whole-line tick bound of one receive equals the idle bound (p3_rectx.c `line_ticks = idle_ticks`; review 2026-09-03 blocker 2 — it was ×4 = 32 s in 734d6c04…): a host line trickled in below the idle gap ends as PARTIAL within P3_BOUND_S, so no wait exceeds 8.0 s on the pinned clock however the bytes are paced; the ×4 factor applies to the poll-count backstop only

schedule.rule: A,B,B,A across successive seed pairs (Claim B prereg §4): candidates 2k and 2k+1 share pair seed k; pair 0 = A,B; pair 1 = B,A; …
schedule.pair_seed: host/l6_schedule.py:PAIR_SEED_RULE — upper 32 bits of the xorshift64 state after 4 steps from ((master_seed<<32) | master_seed) ^ (((pair+1) * golden) mod 2^64), 0 -> golden; twin required in the image
schedule.seq_index: seq 1 = opening baseline, seq i+2 = candidate index i, seq N+2 = closing baseline

operator.derivation: host/l6_operators.py:operator_data over the phenotype manifest + local_map.json: the 292 addresses in genome bit order, each LUT's genome bits in INIT-index order
operator.mutation_bits_note: FROZEN for L6 (owner 2026-09-01), both arms — an image/calibration CONTRACT, not a draft: random-safe = 4 addresses uniform without replacement over the 292; map-guided = one LUT uniform over the map's six, then 4 of its mapped INIT positions. The operator's compute time is inside the rate's `period`, so a calibration holds only for this value; operator_data_sha256 covers mutation_bits and the S runner refuses calibration reports whose operator_data_sha256 is not this pin. If Claim B changes the value, C1/C2 must be re-run under the new contract; the old rates may not be reused.

audit.scheduled: every 16th seq + first and last candidate (seq 2, N+1) + both baselines (seq 1, N+2) — host/l6_schedule.py:sampled_audit_seqs, requested by AUDITREQ
audit.auto: §3a item 2: every non-SCORED self-report (STOP_LINK2, STOP_LINK3, REFUSED_BY_PL, STOP_ARM, STOP_SETTLE, and a post-staging STOP_AXI — one carrying an app_oracle_record) audited unconditionally by the firmware before its record — a firmware change for the §2 image; the validator requires it now (validators.records.check_audit_policy policy='sampled', classification by content in records.self_report_class)
audit.exempt: REFUSED_BY_GATE, and a STOP_AXI that carries no app_oracle_record (pre-staging: no raw words exist). A STOP_AXI WITH an oracle record is a self-report and is auto-audited like the others (validators.records.self_report_class)

frames.crc_budget: ceil(4 × expected_protocol_frames / 1000), expected from N + the audit schedule + the pull-v2 brackets (AUDIT_READY×1 + AUDIT×8 per audited record) BEFORE the session (D-s4, v0.3); any missing AUDIT/REC/TERM is a structural HOLD independently
frames.hb_completeness: exactly 16 HB per SCORED record (baselines included), checked per record by host/l6_checks.py:heartbeat_completeness_findings for C1, C2 and S; fewer or more is a structural HOLD naming the seq

S.n: floor(0.9 × min(planning_C1, planning_C2) × T) — the PLANNING rates of the two v0.6 calibration records (D-t1: candidates over the whole bracketed span, every recovery included), never the inclusive or the nominal rate

sessions.seeds_note: owner 2026-09-01: C1 and C2 share master seed 0x4c364341 (1278624577) so the two calibrations walk the same seed pairs and differ only in the operator; S uses 0x4c36534f (1278628687). S's --duration-s must be exactly 7200 s (a shorter T would shrink both N and the 0.9 T floor). Every L6 (master_seed, index) tuple — hence every pair seed — is EXCLUDED from any future Claim B schedule; the Claim B preregistration must record that exclusion at its freeze. host/l6_runner.py takes the seed from this pin; a --master-seed on the CLI must equal it.

The pull-v2 pins are kept above as explicit historical records and tests prove they cannot be fed to S; no rec-v3 pin ever existed (historical_rec_v3).

historical_rec_v3.note: no rec-v3 calibration exists: C1 #5 (ruling 2026-09-02-01, image 403f4ab5…, prereg v0.4) is HOLD and its rates (3607.8 evals/h inclusive, informational) were never pinned; nothing measured under rec-v3 may budget a v0.6 S (D-r5: the binding names another image/prereg/protocol; D-t2: no planning/inputs)

wire_additions.loop_record: 1.1.0 adds `arm` ∈ {random_safe, map_guided} on candidate records; absent on the two baselines
wire_additions.run_log: adds `timing` (host-written: clocks + per-record stage times) and `l6` (schedule, expected frames, budget inputs)
wire_additions.implemented: firmware/p3_wire.c emits app_identity 1.1.0 and loop_record 1.1.0 (tests/test_firmware_wire_contract.py::L6WireContract feeds the C bytes to the real validator)
wire_additions.rec_transaction: rec-v3 (prereg v0.4 draft): every loop record is a transaction — the board sends REC and waits (bounded) for the host's RECACK (accepted or byte-identical duplicate) or RECGET (arrived broken: resend the same bytes), at most 3 transmissions; unacknowledged → STOP_REC, no next candidate; the host acknowledges only the current candidate (the answered sign exchange whose record is outstanding), refuses a SIGNREQ over an outstanding record and a conflicting duplicate as PROTOCOL; identity page flags.bit4 arms the forced REC-retry control (seq 1's first transmission CRC-corrupted on purpose); app_identity 1.2.0 declares protocol + rec_retry_control; host/l6_rec.py, host/l6_console.py, firmware/p3_rectx.c
wire_additions.rel_transactions: rel-v4 (prereg v0.6, image 5deee74c…): app_identity 1.3.0 (+ sign_retry_control); loop_record 1.1.0 (+ STOP_SIGN with sign_stop); session_summary 1.0.0 (+ closing_control when the control was reached); HB carries {i}; IDENT → IDENTACK, SIGNREQ → SIGNOK|SIGNREF (SIGNGET), AUDIT_READY resent, AUDITWAIT, REC → RECACK|RECGET, TERM → TERMACK (TERMGET); no AUDITREQ frame (audit_requested in SIGNOK); host/l6_rel.py (hosts + twins), host/l6_console.py protocol="rel-v4", firmware/p3_rectx.c p3_tx_run, firmware/p3_pull.c; validators: STOP_SIGN + rule (vii-b); docs/l6_frame_reliability_design.md revision 4

rulings_binding.note: each ruling names the session it authorises and the frozen prereg + pinned image it was issued against; the runner refuses any mismatch, so a C1 ruling cannot run C2 or S and no ruling outlives a re-freeze or a rebuild. --provision-ruling is mandatory: without a P3-K ruling the runner never claims the L6 ruling nor opens the port. l6_manifest_sha256 = the sha256 of THIS file as committed when the ruling was issued: the runner reads the carrier pins, the soak duration and the calibration pins from it, so a swapped manifest with the prereg/image/seed untouched must not pass (closing review blocker 1). C1, C2 and S each bind the manifest hash of their time, since the calibration pins are written between them.

principal_binding.runner_user: == pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_name (the effective UID's name, as the boundary verifier resolves it; never getpass/LOGNAME/USER, which an environment variable can forge — closing review blocker 2)
principal_binding.note: the D4 boundary record is bound to the invocation, not only to itself (board-phase preflight blocker 3)
